sentences.text: Tarascosaurus was a relatively small theropod dinosaur measuring between 2.5 and 3 meters in length, a size inferred from a femur with an estimated undamaged length of 35 centimeters.
However, some sources estimate that Tarascosaurus measured approximately 7 to 9 meters in length.
Tarascosaurus was the first theropod assigned to the Abelisauridae to be discovered in the Northern Hemisphere.
The genus name Tarascosaurus is derived from the Tarasque, a devouring monster from Occitan and Spanish folklore.
The species Tarascosaurus salluvicus was named and described by Buffetaut and Le Loeuff in 1991.
The specific name salluvicus refers to the Salluvii, a Gallic tribe that inhabited the area near Marseille in antiquity.
The holotype specimen PSL 330201 was found in the Fuvelian Beds dating from the lower Campanian stage.
This holotype consists of the upper part of a femur that is 22 centimeters long.
A paratype specimen, PSL 330202, consists of two dorsal vertebrae.
A damaged tail vertebra, specimen PSL 330203, has been referred to the genus.
Tarascosaurus was originally classified within the family Abelisauridae in 1991.
Tarascosaurus is classified within the Abelisauridae due to its straight femoral neck and cavernous structure of the dorsal vertebrae.
Tarascosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 83 to 71 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now Europe.
The time range for Tarascosaurus is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.

In 2003, researchers Allain and Pereda-Suberbiola concluded that the type specimen lacked uniquely abelisaurid traits and should be considered a nomen dubium, a view supported by Oliver Rauhut who argued the available material was not diagnostic.
Phylogenetic analyses conducted in the 2020s support the classification of Tarascosaurus as an abelisaurid.
